ch2_opening.speaker: joseph
ch2_opening.text: Emmanuel. Mama Beata has salt again. Go before it's gone.

ch2_opening.speaker: narrator
ch2_opening.text: Joseph glances at the radio on its stool. It is switched off. It has been off for weeks.

ch2_opening.speaker: joseph
ch2_opening.text: No. People are saying things in the market that they would not have said a year ago. Listen to them. Listen carefully, to who says what, and to who stays quiet.

choices.text: "Why does it matter who says what?"

ch2_opening.speaker: joseph
ch2_opening.text: Because one day you may need to know who you can trust.

ch2_opening.speaker: joseph
ch2_opening.text: And come straight home before dark.

ch2_joseph_day.speaker: joseph
ch2_joseph_day.text: Salt, Emmanuel. And keep your ears open.

ch2_joseph_home.speaker: joseph
ch2_joseph_home.text: You're back. Good. Sit down, Emmanuel. We need to talk.

ch2_beata.speaker: narrator
ch2_beata.text: The shop is half empty. Mama Beata speaks more quietly than she used to.

ch2_beata.speaker: beata
ch2_beata.text: Emmanuel. Come in. Here is your father's salt.

ch2_beata.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_beata.text: The market is so quiet today.

ch2_beata.speaker: beata
ch2_beata.text: Some of my customers have stopped coming. Someone has been telling people which shops they should not buy from.

ch2_beata.speaker: beata
ch2_beata.text: People who want neighbours to stop being neighbours. It starts with small things. Who you buy from. Who you greet.

ch2_beata.speaker: beata
ch2_beata.text: I am a shopkeeper. I am always all right. Mostly.

ch2_beata.speaker: beata
ch2_beata.text: Your father asked you to listen, didn't he? Then listen. Bosco has his radio on at his stall all day. The teacher, Gasana, Claudine: everybody is talking, or trying very hard not to.

ch2_beata.speaker: beata
ch2_beata.text: And Emmanuel, listen more than you speak. These days, words travel.

ch2_beata_default.speaker: beata
ch2_beata_default.text: Go carefully, Emmanuel. Greet your father for me.

ch2_bosco.speaker: narrator
ch2_bosco.text: Bosco's radio sits on his stall between the tomatoes and the onions, turned up loud.

ch2_bosco.speaker: radio
ch2_bosco.text: [The presenter speaks fast and angrily. He says that 'they' are plotting against ordinary people, and that everyone must be ready to defend themselves.]

ch2_bosco.speaker: bosco
ch2_bosco.text: You hear that? Every day it's the same. They say the enemy is already among us. Waiting.

choices.text: "Who is 'the enemy', Bosco? The people you sell tomatoes to?"

ch2_bosco.speaker: bosco
ch2_bosco.text: I'm only repeating what the radio says. Everybody is saying it.

ch2_bosco.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_bosco.text: Everybody repeating something doesn't make it true.

ch2_bosco.speaker: bosco
ch2_bosco.text: You should be careful talking like that, Emmanuel. I'm only telling you because I know your father.

ch2_bosco.speaker: narrator
ch2_bosco.text: Emmanuel says nothing. Bosco nods, as if silence were agreement, and turns the volume up.

ch2_bosco.speaker: narrator
ch2_bosco.text: Around the stall, a few people have stopped to listen. Others hurry past without looking up.

ch2_bosco_default.speaker: bosco
ch2_bosco_default.text: Buy something or move along, Emmanuel. I'm trying to listen.

ch2_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch2_uwase.text: Emmanuel. Have you seen the board? Someone has pinned a notice over the examination timetable.

ch2_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch2_uwase.text: The children come to school repeating what they hear on the radio. Words they don't even understand. Yesterday a boy told another boy he could not sit next to him.

ch2_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch2_uwase.text: I told them what I have always told them. In this classroom there is only one kind of person: a pupil.

ch2_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch2_uwase.text: Some parents have complained. I will not change what I teach.

ch2_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch2_uwase.text: It is not bravery. It is my job. A teacher who repeats lies is not a teacher.

ch2_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch2_uwase.text: Careful is what they want us to be. Careful, and quiet.

ch2_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch2_uwase.text: Think for yourself, Emmanuel. It is the one thing nobody can take from you.

ch2_uwase_default.speaker: uwase
ch2_uwase_default.text: Remember what I told you. Think for yourself.

ch2_gasana.speaker: gasana
ch2_gasana.text: Emmanuel. Sit with an old man for a moment.

ch2_gasana.speaker: gasana
ch2_gasana.text: Two men came by last week. From town, not from here. Very polite. They asked who lives in which house, and they wrote it all down in a little book.

ch2_gasana.speaker: gasana
ch2_gasana.text: Forty years I have lived on this hill. Nobody ever needed a book to know who their neighbours are.

ch2_gasana.speaker: gasana
ch2_gasana.text: They said it was for 'security'. Whose security, I wonder.

ch2_gasana.speaker: gasana
ch2_gasana.text: I told them I am an old man with a very bad memory.

ch2_gasana.speaker: gasana
ch2_gasana.text: Someone is organising this, Emmanuel. Things like this do not happen by themselves.

ch2_gasana_default.speaker: gasana
ch2_gasana_default.text: My memory gets worse every day, Emmanuel. Very convenient.

ch2_claudine.speaker: claudine
ch2_claudine.text: My son still talks about the story you promised him.

ch2_claudine.speaker: claudine
ch2_claudine.text: Some of the other children told him he cannot play with them anymore. Because of what their parents hear on the radio.

ch2_claudine.speaker: claudine
ch2_claudine.text: He asked me what he did wrong. What do I tell a seven-year-old?

choices.text: "Tell him he did nothing wrong. Nothing at all."

ch2_claudine.speaker: claudine
ch2_claudine.text: I tell him that every night. It helps a little less every night.

ch2_claudine.speaker: claudine
ch2_claudine.text: Would you? They listen to you. They always have.

ch2_claudine_default.speaker: claudine
ch2_claudine_default.text: Thank you for stopping. Not everyone stops anymore.

ch2_notice.speaker: narrator
ch2_notice.text: A typed notice has been pinned to the board, right over the old examination timetable.

ch2_notice.speaker: narrator
ch2_notice.text: COMMUNITY MEETING. Saturday, at the trading centre. All young men are expected to attend. Absence will be noted.

ch2_notice.speaker: narrator
ch2_notice.text: Someone has torn away half of the examination timetable to make room.

ch2_aline_early.speaker: aline
ch2_aline_early.text: Emmanuel? Finish your father's errand first. I'll still be here.

ch2_aline.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_aline.text: You always come up here when something is wrong.

ch2_aline.speaker: aline
ch2_aline.text: At the market today, a woman I have known since I was a baby looked straight through me. As if I wasn't there.

ch2_aline.speaker: aline
ch2_aline.text: My father says we should carry our identity cards with us at all times now. As if a card could explain who a person is.

choices.text: "Your card never mattered to me. It never will."

ch2_aline.speaker: aline
ch2_aline.text: I know. That's why I came up here to wait for you.

ch2_aline.speaker: aline
ch2_aline.text: So am I. Being afraid is not the same as giving up. My mother taught me that.

ch2_aline.speaker: aline
ch2_aline.text: My brother doesn't understand any of it. Yesterday he asked why some of the boys won't pass him the ball anymore.

ch2_aline.speaker: aline
ch2_aline.text: That some people are listening to the wrong things.

ch2_aline.speaker: aline
ch2_aline.text: Emmanuel, Patrick was looking for you. He was with two men I've never seen before. He said he'd wait at the football field.

ch2_aline_after.speaker: aline
ch2_aline_after.text: Go and see what Patrick wants. And Emmanuel, be careful what you promise him.

ch2_patrick_early.speaker: patrick
ch2_patrick_early.text: Not now, Emmanuel. Later. We'll talk later.

ch2_patrick.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_patrick.text: Aline said you were looking for me. Who are those men?

ch2_patrick.speaker: patrick
ch2_patrick.text: Friends. People who are finally organising things properly.

ch2_patrick.speaker: patrick
ch2_patrick.text: Things are changing. People are choosing sides. If you're not with us, they will consider you against us.

ch2_patrick.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_patrick.text: Aline is my friend. You know that.

ch2_patrick.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_patrick.text: Then we should be protecting one another, not turning on one another.

ch2_patrick.speaker: patrick
ch2_patrick.text: There's a meeting on Saturday at the trading centre. Everyone will see who comes. And who doesn't.

choices.text: [Refuse] "I won't be there. Not on Saturday. Not ever."
[Pretend to go along] "…All right. I'll think about it."

ch2_patrick.speaker: patrick
ch2_patrick.text: Then you've chosen. Remember that I tried to help you.

ch2_patrick.speaker: narrator
ch2_patrick.text: Emmanuel says nothing. Patrick studies his face for a long moment.

ch2_patrick.speaker: patrick
ch2_patrick.text: Silence is an answer too. They will decide what it means.

ch2_patrick.speaker: narrator
ch2_patrick.text: The words feel wrong even as Emmanuel says them. Patrick claps him on the shoulder.

ch2_patrick.speaker: patrick
ch2_patrick.text: Good. That's smart. Smart people will be safe.

ch2_patrick.speaker: patrick
ch2_patrick.text: Go home, Emmanuel. It will be dark soon.

ch2_didier.speaker: didier
ch2_didier.text: Kevin's father says we can't play with Eric and Grace anymore. Because of the radio.

choices.text: "On this field, everyone plays. That's the rule."

ch2_didier.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_didier.text: Says the person who's going to bring a pump for that flat ball.

ch2_didier.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_didier.text: A real pump. Eric! Grace! Come on, you're on Didier's team.

ch2_didier.speaker: narrator
ch2_didier.text: For a little while, the children play together again, as if nothing has changed.

ch2_evening.speaker: narrator
ch2_evening.text: The radio stays silent on its stool.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: Men came to the house today. They said a man who once led this community should lead it again, at the meetings.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: They said there will be 'work' to do soon, and that everyone must take part.
ch2_evening.text_reduced: They said everyone must take part in what is coming.

ch2_evening.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_evening.text: What did you tell them?

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: That my knees are old and my heart is older. And that I do not do that kind of work.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: They did not like that answer. They will come back.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: Now. What did you hear today?

ch2_evening.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_evening.text: Gasana says men from town came and wrote down names. Which families live in which house.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: Then it is worse than I thought.

ch2_evening.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_evening.text: There's a notice at the school. A meeting on Saturday. It says absence will be noted.

ch2_evening.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_evening.text: Patrick wants me at that meeting. I told him no.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: Good. Saying no has a price these days. We will pay it quietly, and together.

ch2_evening.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_evening.text: Patrick wants me at that meeting. I didn't answer him.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: Silence keeps you safe for a day. It does not keep anyone else safe. Think about that.

ch2_evening.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_evening.text: Patrick wants me at that meeting. I told him I'd think about it.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: You let him believe you might go.

ch2_evening.speaker: emmanuel
ch2_evening.text: I didn't know what else to say.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: Sometimes a lie buys time. Just never let the lie become who you are. Pretending is not joining. See that it never becomes joining.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: Emmanuel. Listen to me now.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: If one day someone knocks on our door asking for help, we open it. Do you understand me?

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: Especially then.

ch2_evening.speaker: joseph
ch2_evening.text: Go and sleep. And say nothing about this to anyone.
